seating.note: Highest margin — chair is always the most negotiable item for client but shouldn't be for TCD

receptionStations.note: High brand impact, high margin, client rarely challenges reception pricing

boardroomTables.note: Statement piece — clients invest here more willingly than workstations

executiveDesks.note: GOJO Vol 2 commands premium margin — never discount without value case

sitStandDesks.note: Higher margin than fixed desks — premium ergonomic positioning protects price

workstations.note: Volume category — margin protected by installation revenue alongside

storage.note: Lowest margin but builds order value and lock-in

installation.note: High-margin service line — never discount installation

marginProtectionRules: Never discount before the full value case is presented — discounting early signals inflated pricing
If discounting, always trade for a commitment: 'If I get approval for that reduction, can we confirm by Friday?'
Add value before reducing price: extra chair, extended warranty registration, disposal of old furniture
Installation and delivery margin is non-negotiable — it covers labour risk and site management
Packaging and logistics costs are real — never absorb these to win a deal
marginErosionWarnings: Scope creep without re-quoting — absorbing client additions silently destroys margin
Last-minute finish changes — manufacturer re-runs cost real money
Rushed delivery without a logistics premium — expedited freight doubles cost
Unsupported discounting — the CEO must approve any discount above 5%
Underestimating installation time — complex builds take longer than simple estimates

marginCalculationPrinciple.COGS: Product landed cost + delivery cost + installation labour + any third-party costs
marginCalculationPrinciple.targetCheck: Before confirming any project, calculate blended GM across all line items. If below 28%, escalate for approval.
